summary: This report profiles local inventors and entrepreneurs whose projects, launched between September and December 2023, are building the local smart city. It covers environmental sensing, IoT infrastructure, transportation, energy, health and safety, smart homes, civic participation, and education. The central point is that local innovators are turning smart city ideas into real applications.
one_line: A report on local inventors whose 2023 smart city projects span IoT, transportation, energy, health, housing, civic participation and education.
key_facts: Alicia Martinez's startup GreenCanopy deployed sensor-laden smart trees on September 15, 2023; they provide shade and air purification and monitor environmental data.
Tony Huang created "RecycleGo," introduced October 3, 2023, which gamifies recycling for citizens.
Dr. Sarah Kim's team unveiled "LightGrid" on November 12, 2023, a network of streetlights that communicates about traffic, weather and energy consumption and adjusts lighting in real time.
Raj Patel, a water resource specialist, designed the "AquaNet" system, launched September 30, 2023, which uses sensors across urban waterways to monitor water quality.
Mia Zhang introduced an AI-driven traffic management platform on October 21, 2023 that integrates with personal navigation devices and city infrastructure to reduce congestion.
Alex Johnson piloted the electric mini-bus fleet "E-Commute" on December 5, 2023, which operates dynamically based on commuter demand.
Dr. Lina Rodriguez's "SolarSkin" project, unveiled September 20, 2023, is a photovoltaic film that adheres to building exteriors to generate power.
Jake Simmons launched the "SmartGrid" system on November 15, 2023, letting homes and businesses monitor energy use and trade surplus energy.
Lydia Chen's crowdsourced "SafeWalk" app, released September 22, 2023, provides real-time safety information.
Dr. Keith Franklin's "HealthSpot" kiosks have been deployed in public venues since October 10, 2023, giving immediate health feedback and linking to local health services.

Sophia Wallace introduced "EcoHabitats," intelligent homes that interact with the urban ecosystem, on November 28, 2023; Omar Bradley's AI-based "IntelliHome" system was introduced September 29, 2023.
Michael Anderson's "CivicSense" project, unveiled October 25, 2023, builds tools for public input into city planning.
Sandra Lo has been general counsel to the city's technology department since September 1, 2023, crafting "tech-friendly" legislation that addresses privacy and security.

Clara Johnson introduced a digital literacy and smart technology curriculum in public schools on November 20, 2023, and Mark Schmidt's "TechTrade" workshops began December 1, 2023 to upskill local workers.
